mcq.s: Which of the following statements about the Param Vir Chakra is correct?
o: It can be awarded to an individual only once in a lifetime
Its medal bears four replicas of Indra's Vajra
It has so far been awarded to 25 persons
mcq.x: The Param Vir Chakra, India's highest wartime gallantry award, was instituted on 26 January 1950 and its medal bears four replicas of Indra's Vajra. A bar allows a second award, and only 21 persons have received it.

mcq.s: Who among the following was a recipient of the Bharat Ratna for 2024?
mcq.x: The 2024 Bharat Ratna went to five persons: Karpoori Thakur, L.K. Advani, P.V. Narasimha Rao, Chaudhary Charan Singh and M.S. Swaminathan. Pranab Mukherjee got it in 2019 and C.N.R. Rao in 2014.

mcq.s: Who among the following was among the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna?
mcq.x: The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954; its first recipients that year were C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman. Nehru got it in 1955, Rajendra Prasad in 1962 and Shastri in 1966.

mcq.s: What is the correct chronological order of the following? 1. Shimla Agreement 2. Indo-Soviet Treaty 3. Farakka Accord 4. Tashkent Agreement
mcq.x: Tashkent Declaration (January 1966), Indo-Soviet Treaty of Friendship (August 1971), Shimla Agreement (July 1972) and the Farakka Accord with Bangladesh (1977; final Ganga treaty 1996).

mcq.s: Who is the author of the books 'The India Way' and 'Why Bharat Matters'?
mcq.x: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar wrote 'The India Way: Strategies for an Uncertain World' (2020) and 'Why Bharat Matters' (2024).

mcq.s: Who launched the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign on the occasion of India's 75th Independence Day?
mcq.x: Har Ghar Tiranga was launched by the Central Government (Ministry of Culture) in 2022 under Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, and is held every year around Independence Day.

mcq.s: Which of the following are members of the Arctic Council? 1. Denmark 2. Japan 3. Russian Federation 4. United Kingdom 5. United States of America
mcq.x: The Arctic Council (Ottawa Declaration, 1996) has eight members: Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden and the USA. India, Japan and the UK are only observers.

mcq.s: The term 'Yavanapriya', mentioned in ancient Sanskrit texts, denoted
o: a fine variety of Indian muslin
damsels sent to the Greek court for dance performance
mcq.x: Yavanapriya ('dear to the Yavanas') was black pepper, a chief export of the Indo-Roman trade.

mcq.s: Match List I (Year) with List II (Event): I. 1883 II. 1906 III. 1927 IV. 1932 — A. Announcement of the Communal Award B. Formation of the All-India States Peoples' Conference C. Foundation of the Muslim League at Dacca D. First session of the National Conference at Calcutta
mcq.x: Indian National Conference first met at Calcutta in 1883, the Muslim League was founded at Dacca in 1906, the All-India States Peoples' Conference was formed in 1927 and the Communal Award came in 1932.

mcq.s: Consider the following landmarks in Indian education: 1. Hindu College, Calcutta 2. University of Calcutta 3. Adam's Report 4. Wood's Despatch. What is their correct chronological order?
mcq.x: Hindu College (1817), Adam's Reports on vernacular education in Bengal and Bihar (1835-38), Wood's Despatch (1854) and the University of Calcutta (1857).
